findings.title: One reminder for each open School choice
findings.status: Owner ruled the direction; Q1 settles unique reminders
findings.observed: Kuni and Matsu repeat free-Skill findings in the top Still to choose box and the cards. The monk capture also contains a Lore-subject and three-Kiho reminder only in that box; those are not duplicates.
findings.impact: Removing the whole box blindly would lose unfinished work.
findings.proposal: Keep the sheet cards as ruled. Suppress only matching duplicate findings; move unique Lore, Kiho or other open-choice reminders into the same card presentation. Keep XP overspend and Finish confirmation unchanged. Coordinate with 8b/8c provenance; do not implement those pickers here.

findings.title: Floating controls cover the sheet
findings.observed: At 390 px the Quick Access circle overlays section titles; the return-to-top control competes with the bottom tabs and the dice launcher covers lower content. Search already has a persistent app-bar entry.
findings.impact: Headings and controls lose space exactly where the phone has least room.
findings.proposal: Reserve one compact Quick Access/Dice action strip above the bottom tabs with content padding and safe-area allowance. Show one return-to-top control only after scrolling; no extra destination bar. Preserve existing shortcuts, page position and tab behavior.

findings.title: Top-align columns and simplify long Skill cards
findings.observed: With unequal lists the desktop Advantage column begins far below the Disadvantage column. Phone Skill rows spend much of a viewport on repeated scaffolding and notes.
findings.impact: Unnecessary scrolling makes related entries difficult to compare.
findings.proposal: Top-align both columns. Give phone Skill cards a compact name/rank/roll row with secondary editing and Mastery details under a labelled disclosure; retain every value, School tick and action. Do not move Management into another screen.

findings.title: A single accessible information pattern
findings.observed: Gold italic I, circled i, eye and question-mark treatments coexist. Hotei repeats summary, rule explanation and manual-action text. Inspection also found information buttons nested inside configuration buttons.
findings.impact: Repeated prose hides state; nested buttons make keyboard and touch behavior ambiguous.
findings.proposal: Use the existing upright circled i for reference detail on Skills, spells, Advantages and Disadvantages. Make it a sibling button with an accessible name and adequate touch area. Keep selection, cost, current state, unpaid/disabled reasons and actionable warnings visible; put static explanation behind the disclosure. Keep Help/Why cannot I cast semantics distinct where they explain an error.

findings.title: Make the limb picker fit the shared controls
findings.observed: Missing Limb uses a small native select beside larger sheet buttons.
findings.impact: The field reads as an unrelated widget and is hard to hit.
findings.proposal: Keep the native select, with the shared label, spacing, font and touch height. Do not add a custom menu for a short finite list.

findings.title: Separate grant actions and their state
findings.observed: Add koku and Already added sit against one another and compete for emphasis. Wealthy shares the grant pattern.
findings.impact: A state acknowledgement looks like another equally important grant action.
findings.proposal: Use a compact action group with a clear gap: primary Add N koku, secondary Already added. Show granted state beside it, retain the one-time guard and reversal behavior, keep touch targets large.

findings.title: Align the Moon row
findings.observed: Full moon tonight, Medium and Change sit on different visual baselines.
findings.impact: The setting and the session toggle are difficult to scan as one entry.
findings.proposal: Use a labelled severity row and a separate aligned full-moon toggle; preserve Resist Lord Moon (TN n), state, extra-pip order and all rules.

findings.title: Undo a burst of quick point changes
findings.status: Owner ruled grouping; Q4 fixes boundary
findings.observed: Measured Honor 4 + 7 points, three quick + taps, then Undo: it returns to 4 + 9 and Undo disappears. Only the last tap is reverted.
findings.impact: An accidental burst needs several reversals but only one is available.
findings.proposal: Group consecutive minus/plus taps on the same characteristic with a rolling five-second gap. Undo restores the value before the first tap. A different card, typed adjustment, recognition, open/save transition or unrelated action ends the group. Keep one coherent History change and matching undo record; pin boundary cases.

findings.title: Phone text entry and repeated taps
findings.observed: Rank and Points inputs measured 14 px; adjustment input 16 px. Steppers measured 44 × 44 with touch-action:auto. The iPhone zoom failures are owner reports, not reproduced in Chromium.
findings.impact: Small input text and default repeated-tap behavior are plausible contributors; the stuck zoom-out case remains unexplained.
findings.proposal: Use at least 16 px editable input text on phones and touch-action:manipulation on buttons/steppers only. Preserve pinch zoom and ordinary double-tap zoom elsewhere. Validate all three reported cases on Safari and the installed iPhone app before calling FT-49 fixed; do not force-reset viewport scale.

findings.title: Cross-page actions must move focus
findings.observed: Owner reported the Advanced School button below its hint baseline and focus remaining on Identity. Source inspection confirms AP7.go scrolls Techniques but never moves focus. The dense audit fixture does not meet an Advanced School prerequisite, so the button is hidden in these screenshots.
findings.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users can remain on the old page after navigation.
findings.proposal: Centre the hint and compact desktop button in a wrapping row; retain 44 px touch height. On every cross-page action, focus the destination heading after carousel settlement, without reopening the keyboard. Test source-page inertness and return navigation.

findings.title: Space explanatory text below fields
findings.observed: Insight and Spent XP explanations sit hard against the fields above.
findings.impact: Labels, values and supporting notes blend together.
findings.proposal: Apply a shared small helper-text gap and readable line height to these field groups, then inspect equivalent groups across the sheet.

findings.title: Collapse resistance choices into one line
findings.observed: Honor resistance choices for Intimidation, Temptation and Fear consume several lines in the roll preview.
findings.impact: Situational choices overwhelm the roll being prepared.
findings.proposal: One initially closed Resisting? disclosure, with selected state/count visible in its summary. Expand to the existing labelled choices; preserve all bonus calculations, exclusivity and reset behavior. A selected resistance must never become invisible.

findings.title: Keep campaign wounds beside Earth
findings.observed: Campaign multipliers and the threshold preview are beside Earth in Manage. Combat is a Play-only page.
findings.impact: Moving the editor to Combat would cut across the accepted mode split.
findings.proposal: Retain the editor and preview here; keep Combat’s plain pointer to Rings & Traits. Revisit location only if the later separate-Manage review changes the mode structure. No second editable copy.

findings.title: Explain wound penalties once
findings.observed: The owner’s two-wound-entry example is correct but confusing; current dense captures cover the track, not that exact two-entry state.
findings.impact: Base rank penalty and modifiers can be mistaken for one another.
findings.proposal: Use one net penalty on the track and an info breakdown showing rank penalty, each signed modifier and total. Preserve the existing arithmetic and reduced-penalty floors. Add the owner’s two-entry fixture before building; this is presentation only.

findings.title: Court chips should be direct controls
findings.observed: The row has court chips alongside the configuration action; adding a court requires entering the editor.
findings.impact: The visual chip suggests an action without a consistently sized target.
findings.proposal: Make each whole chip a labelled selection button; place Add court on the row. Keep rename/remove in the editor and retain the selected/in-session state.

findings.title: Remove the redundant bottom information button
findings.observed: The older device pass identified a bottom i duplicating option text and the row’s info control. Current representative pickers still mix reference and configuration controls.
findings.impact: A generic extra information action adds visual noise without a clear subject.
findings.proposal: Remove the redundant bottom i only from the seven identified legacy pickers; keep option explanations and row information. Inventory those seven against their historical test IDs before editing, and retain a single accessible way to every explanation.

findings.title: Fill the splash without cutting off the title
findings.observed: The image uses object-fit:contain. This phone ratio nearly matches the portrait image; owner evidence records paper bands at other phone/laptop ratios.
findings.impact: Presentation changes with aspect ratio, especially desktop and rotation.
findings.proposal: Use cover with separate portrait/landscape focal positions that keep the seal/title in view, or a matching edge extension if cover cannot preserve them. Test 390×844, 844×390, 1536×864 and narrow landscape. Keep first-paint coverage and readiness/error dismissal exactly as shipped.

findings.title: Investigate the first Manage tap on an iPhone
findings.observed: The historical iPhone delay was not measurable in prior headless tests. This desktop Chromium audit does not reproduce an iPhone timing failure.
findings.impact: A cosmetic rewrite without a reproduction could add risk and solve nothing.
findings.proposal: Reserve a bounded instrumented native-device check: input event to mode-painted frame on first and second taps, same character. Fix only a demonstrated bottleneck. If it does not recur, close as not reproduced with the measurements; no arbitrary delay or full mode redesign.

findings.title: Undo the most recent Void-card spend
findings.status: Design ruled 9 October; Q7 approves inclusion
findings.observed: The parked functional request is wider than layout: card spending has no single action that restores the pip, removes its bonus and drops its pending Willpower roll. The screenshots are context, not a new failure reproduction.
findings.impact: A mistaken spend is difficult to reverse safely.
findings.proposal: A separate removable functional layer: Undo the latest card spend until the next roll, Next Round or Reset. Restore the exact resource and pending effect once, including Touch of the Void. Do not conflate this with an after-preview refund or general History undo. Pin invalidation and double-undo cases.

findings.title: Choose a Trait for one Skill roll
findings.status: Parked by owner; Q7 approves exact scope
findings.observed: The Skill row rolls its default Trait; alternate pairings were documented in the existing Skill Traits audit. No new sourcebook ruling was made here.
findings.impact: Players must switch to the generic dice tray for an alternate pairing.
findings.proposal: An optional Trait selector in the Skill roll preview for that roll only, defaulting to the accepted catalogue Trait. Clearly label a nondefault choice, reset on next opening, preserve Skill/emphasis/unskilled modifiers. Do not change saved Skill data or calculate career XP. Re-read AUDIT — Skill Traits and the cited pages before implementing any rule-dependent behavior.

findings.title: Use short thematic check labels
findings.observed: Generic Check labels and inconsistent phrasing obscure the action’s purpose.
findings.impact: A player must reread the entry before pressing a routine button.
findings.proposal: Proposed labels: Brash — Resist insult; Overconfident — Measure the enemy; Can’t Lie — Discretion check; Contrary — Cooperate; Rumormonger — Resist gossip; Soft-Hearted — Resolve check; Lost Love — Steady yourself — Spend Void. Keep TN visible and retain all mechanical conditions and costs.

findings.title: State actual and catalogue price consistently
findings.observed: The owner recorded inconsistent changed-price wording for Social Position and Kharmic Tie with Blissful Betrothal. The synthetic dense fixture is not a pricing-rules proof.
findings.impact: The player cannot easily tell whether a displayed cost includes the discount.
findings.proposal: Use Actual N XP · catalogue M XP with the reason in information detail, consistently with Clan-priced rows. Read the existing price engine’s outputs; do not recompute or change prices in this layer.

findings.title: Give Leadership a concise action label
findings.observed: Leadership’s action includes the long School Rank + 1k1 formula as well as descriptive text.
findings.impact: The button is difficult to scan at phone width.
findings.proposal: Label it Lead an ally. Put the formula and use condition beside it or in its information detail, while keeping any required current amount visible before activation.

findings.title: Avoid repeating Blind under Armor TN
findings.observed: Quick Access adds a Blind explanation below Armor TN, whose existing breakdown already explains the base.
findings.impact: The same rule competes with the current value.
findings.proposal: Remove only the duplicate line once the Armor TN information exposes the complete Blind contribution; keep the value and a clearly reachable breakdown.

findings.title: Keep success wording restrained
findings.observed: You keep your head is the owner-reported Touch of the Void success wording. The roll-preview image is context; no random success was forced for this audit.
findings.impact: Its tone differs from the surrounding rules feedback.
findings.proposal: Use You remain in control. Preserve the roll result, TN, failure condition and cost messages.

findings.title: Reduce repeated Clan and School prose
findings.observed: The page repeats School identity, application guidance and reference prose around its controls.
findings.impact: The player has to work through the same context before finding an action.
findings.proposal: Keep one identity summary and one Apply/Cancel instruction in Manage; place background/reference prose behind information. Play retains the selected School and useful Technique link. Do not remove pending-change or School-choice warnings.

findings.title: Keep Search controls reachable while scrolling
findings.observed: Deep result scrolling loses the query and filters while the app bar remains at the top. Search already exists in that bar, so another global destination bar would duplicate it.
findings.impact: Changing a query requires returning through a long list.
findings.proposal: A compact sticky query/category region within Search, optional filters in a disclosure, and a return-to-top action in that region. Keep result scroll and focus restoration when closing a detail. Retain the existing global Search entry; decline a second bottom navigation bar.

findings.title: Clarify Search facets without discarding useful filters
findings.observed: Cost has equal prominence to primary facets. Weapon Type is Weapon/Arrow rather than a kind, while Skill already groups kinds. Clans and Families are mixed.
findings.impact: Filters take space and their labels do not always match the user’s question.
findings.proposal: Move Cost into More filters, retaining its capability. Use Skill as the primary weapon-kind filter and label the existing Weapon/Arrow discriminator Item type in More filters. Add All / Clans / Families. Preserve combinations, counts and clear/reset behavior.

findings.title: Refresh Skill picker Trait labels
findings.observed: The owner recorded Intimidation labelled Willpower in the picker while its added row uses Awareness. Current row captured; this audit did not recapture the open picker label.
findings.impact: Conflicting labels undermine trust even when the roll is correct.
findings.proposal: Generate picker labels from the final corrected catalogue, after later layers apply. Compare every picker Trait to its resulting row; change labels only. Keep this independent of FT-28.

findings.title: Remove old-name tags but retain search aliases
findings.status: Tag removal requested; Q5 retains aliases
findings.observed: Formerly labels are still displayed for the two renamed spells.
findings.impact: Migration wording keeps taking room after the correction is familiar.
findings.proposal: Hide Formerly tags in results and details, retaining both old names as search aliases and old-save/scroll compatibility. The Spell Names test’s display assertion will need a switch-aware expectation with its count unchanged; the alias checks must stay.

findings.title: Search must say four different Blackmail targets
findings.observed: Search lists Blackmail (Advantage), while the School picker’s accepted requirement is four different people.
findings.impact: A player preparing for the School sees an incomplete requirement.
findings.proposal: Use the accepted picker’s four-different-people wording in Search with the existing citation. Do not alter eligibility, counting, or reintroduce the removed confirmation.

findings.title: Make browser print complete and compact
findings.observed: The dense browser PDF has 8 pages: large gaps, an overwide Rings row, an empty Skills Roll column and screen actions on paper. The long weapon name and notes now wrap; the old clipping failure was not reproduced. The 7-page template PDF uses continuation references for overflow.
findings.impact: Paper is wasted and interactive controls look like character information.
findings.proposal: Fix Rings width first; hide actions, spinners, empty Roll columns and screen-only instructions while retaining character state. Top-align Advantage columns, avoid unnecessary forced page breaks and suppress truly empty panels. Guard long weapon/notes and all carried state. No fixed page-count target: complete readable output wins. Preserve the accepted template and its continuation pages; do not compress its intentional writing space.

findings.title: Move and update the colophon
findings.observed: Browser print still carries the old Part E build line and backup guidance; the colophon adds competing text near navigation.
findings.impact: Obsolete build wording makes the current release look stale.
findings.proposal: Put current provenance/credits in About from the existing menu, remove stale or screen-only copy from print, and preserve required attribution/license content in an accessible location. Avoid adding another floating control.

findings.title: Separate Jigoku’s total from its calculation
findings.observed: The historical device pass proposed a clearer Lost label; the dense fixture did not include Jigoku and this wording was not freshly reproduced.
findings.impact: A condition label and the arithmetic should be distinguishable.
findings.proposal: Use +8 to total — Taint Rank 4 × 2 (Lost) for that example, generated from current values; never hard-code 8 or Rank 4. Preserve the actual formula and gate.

findings.title: Retain the Library’s book correction dropdown
findings.observed: The native correction select has 16 named books plus Another book. It fits this screen and the recognition/Change flow matches the agreed mock-up. The imported PDF was a synthetic test fixture.
findings.impact: A second custom search picker adds complexity without evidence that this finite list is hard to use.
findings.proposal: Keep the dropdown and recognition summary; revisit a searchable picker if the catalogue grows substantially or native-device use shows a problem. The broader mock-up change list is already implemented, so do not reopen it as Phase 15 work.

findings.title: Keep a citation range together
findings.observed: The Not in Library badge interrupts the displayed page range between pp.249 and -250.
findings.impact: The reference becomes harder to read and can look like two separate citations.
findings.proposal: Render the whole book/page-range link, then its Library state badge as a sibling. Keep the link destination and missing-book action unchanged.

rulings: Q1
Approve the proposed scopes, not a build start

15a includes the listed layout/control work and unique Review reminders; 15b includes the listed text/Search/browser-print work. Preserve every warning, state and rule called out above. Estimates below include release QA and rollback. 8b and 8c remain ahead of both; approval here does not authorize either implementation or a merge.
Q2
Use one navigation system

Reserve a compact action strip above the existing tabs; keep Search in the app bar; make Search’s own query/category region sticky; move the colophon to About. No second destination bar or separate Manage screen.
Q3
Adopt one information/disclosure treatment

Upright circled i as a separate labelled control, static prose behind it, live state and reasons visible. Whole court chips select; Add court sits on the row; remove only the redundant bottom i in the seven legacy pickers.
Q4
Use a rolling five-second Undo group

Same characteristic’s consecutive −/+ taps are one change until five seconds without a tap or another action ends the group. Restore the value before the first tap and record the grouped change consistently in History.
Q5
Keep useful capability with simpler presentation

Keep wounds beside Earth, the current Library dropdown, former-spell search aliases and Cost/Weapon–Arrow filters under More filters. Add a Clan/Family split. These are the explicit retain/decline calls.
Q6
Fill the splash while preserving the title
Approve cover with tested portrait/landscape focal positioning; if the title cannot fit an extreme ratio, extend matching edges rather than crop the title. Retain all startup safeguards.
Q7
Include the two bounded functional items in 15a

Include FT-24’s already-ruled Void spend Undo and FT-28’s one-roll Trait choice as separate removable layers. They account for 5 planning points (range 3–7) within 15a; deferring both reduces 15a’s centre estimate from 20 to 15.
Q8
Approve the wording set

Use B01’s seven action labels, Lead an ally, You remain in control, the actual/catalogue cost pattern, Blind’s single breakdown and the value-driven Jigoku line. Keep TNs, prices, eligibility and costs intact.

approval.notice: Owner accepted Q1–Q8 as recommended on 1 November 2026. The approved Phase 15 delivery rules govern implementation: one independently removable finding at a time, owner testing/acceptance before progression, all 15a before 15b, and removal of any finding/group/phase preserves retained work and character data. A13/B15 are accepted retain-current-design decisions; A19/FT-24 and A20/FT-28 are included. Earlier grouped-delivery estimates require revision. Q1–Q8 are settled and must not be asked again without a material change. Implementation has not started; the 8b/8c work order remains in place.
